title: The pyramids of Giza
examples: What was the purpose of building the pyramids?
Can you tell me more about the people who built them?
Were the pyramids always as big as they are now?

explain.say: Today we will learn about the great pyramids of Giza.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the pyramids of Giza. Look at the great pyramid, the pyramid of khafre and the casing stones. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The largest pyramid was built for a pharaoh named Khufu.
These massive structures were built around the year 2560 before common era.
Archaeologists suggest that large ramps were used to help lift the stones.
The pyramids were once considered one of the great wonders of the ancient world.
Think about building a very tall sandcastle on the beach.

faq.q: Why were the pyramids built so large?
faq.a: They were built to serve as tombs for the pharaohs. The pharaohs were considered very important rulers.
asks: What was the purpose of the pyramids?
Who did the pyramids belong to?

faq.a: Current understanding suggests the workers were skilled laborers who were paid. They were organized workers, not slaves.

faq.q: How did they move the heavy stones?
faq.a: They likely used sledges pulled over wet ground or ramps. This helped reduce the friction on the heavy loads.
asks: Did they use wheels for everything?

faq.q: Are all the pyramids at Giza the same?
faq.a: No, they vary in size and construction. Khufu's pyramid is the largest and most famous one.
asks: Are there different types of pyramids?

faq.a: The main construction period was around 2560 before common era. This places them in the Old Kingdom period.

facts: The Great Pyramid was built for the Pharaoh Khufu.
Its construction date is estimated around 2560 before common era.
Workers used ramps and sledges to move the huge blocks.
The pyramids were once among the world's great wonders.

quiz.say: The pyramids were mainly built to serve as:
quiz.why: The pyramids were constructed primarily as elaborate burial places for the pharaohs.

wrong.1: A temple was a place for worship, but the pyramid itself was a tomb structure.
wrong.2: A marketplace was for trade, which is a different function entirely.
wrong.3: A palace was a residence for living, not a final resting place.

quiz.say: The construction process involved moving heavy stones using:
quiz.why: Evidence suggests that ramps were a key method for raising the massive stone blocks into place.

wrong.1: While impressive, the construction required massive amounts of human effort and engineering.
wrong.2: Water currents were not a practical way to lift stones to such heights.
wrong.3: Rolling alone would not provide enough upward force for the sheer weight.

quiz.say: If you compare the pyramid's purpose to a modern building, it was most like:
quiz.why: Its primary function was as a monumental, permanent burial structure for royalty.

wrong.1: A museum displays artifacts, but the pyramid's core purpose was burial.
wrong.2: A school is for learning, whereas the pyramid was for eternal rest.
wrong.3: An office is for administration, not for royal burial.
